title: Daily NR7 compression day, next-day upside breakout on 1h in 50-day uptrend

source.title: NR4/NR7 Narrow-range Bars
source.license: Free to use with attribution (LuxAlgo Library)

rule_summary: Daily signals from closed UTC daily candles built from 1h data; execution on 1h. A day D is NR7 when its high-low range is strictly smaller than the high-low range of each of the 6 days before it. The day after D (UTC), if the last closed daily close is above the SMA(50) of daily closes, ENTRY on the first 1h bar whose close is above the NR7 day's high (order at next 1h open), only if that bar closes before 20:00 UTC. At most one entry per NR7 day. EXIT at a 1h close below the NR7 day's low, or after 48 1h bars from entry (time exit), whichever comes first. Hard stop at the NR7 day's low (checked on closed bars). Enter nothing on days that are not the day after an NR7 day. No take-profit, no pyramiding.
mechanism: A very narrow day means participants agreed on price and resting stop orders and breakout orders stack just beyond the range. When price clears the high, short covering and momentum buyers must buy at once, so the following move tends to exceed the narrow range. The sellers who give the money away are those who faded the range and are stopped out. The source gives no mechanism beyond compression-then-expansion; this is the closest honest one. Cost risk: the stop is the narrow range, so the target must be larger than 0.35%.
